text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the opposition rightist Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) held conventions on Sunday officially starting their parliamentary campaigns.

DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI - The ruling coalition of the SLD and the Polish Peasants Party (PSL) is responsible for the low priority status assigned to health protection reform and for keeping bad insurance laws, centrist opposition Union for Freedom (UW) front-bencher Marek Balicki said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's most secure, effective and competitive banks are now Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), Bank Slaski (BSK), Bank Handlowy and PKO BP, a report by the Gdansk Market Research Institute (IBnGR) said.
- Around 56 percent of Poles have declared savings and other forms of investments, a February 1997 survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- Trucks will be permitted to drive in Poland only from 11 PM until 11 AM from July 2 whenver daytime temperature exceeds 30 degrees centigrade.
- The Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms monopolist, has contracted Alcatel telephone exchanges worth eight million European Currency Units (ECU).
- Poland's strawberry harvests will show a 30 percent decline compared with 1996, the agricultural sector's state supervision and monitoring body said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Foreign investments by Polish firms declined by 60 percent in the period between 1994 and 1996, the central bank's hard currency reserve department said.
- Poland's access to the EU will force the consolidation of brokerage houses, IB Austria Polish branch director Jacek Krawczyk said.
- Only 18 percent of Poles will go away on holiday this year, a survey by the Demoskop polling institute said.
- Provincial authorities have formed a new wholesale commodity exchange in the Bielsko Biala province, southern Poland, with a share capital of 750,000 zlotys.
The industries located in the province account for four percent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP).
- The PDPS PZL glider maker in Bielsko Biala will be privatised in July this year to help the firm pay its debts, the plant's director Jerzy Oleszkiewicz said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Belchatow brown coal mine will not sell its 12.2 percent stake in Petrobank, which it planned to do following a management dispute with the bank's major shareholder, the South Korean LG Group, Belchatow and LG Group agreed.
ZYCIE
- The EU will cut import duties for Polish agricultural products as of July 1, which may increase exports by up to $10 million annually, the Food and Agricultural Economy Institute (IERiGZ) said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
